brief: MS raises its 12-month S&P 500 target to 8,700 (19x 2028 EPS of $458). It sees 2026 EPS of $369 (34% growth), 2027 EPS of $420 (14%) and 2028 EPS of $458 (9%). The call rests on a chain: the April 2025 earnings recovery is maturing into a stable mid-cycle phase as Fed policy normalizes toward less accommodation, which drove a correction MS flagged in June (a call to underperform Semis) that pushed the index down to narrow breadth. That process is now advanced, with the S&P near MS's 7,100-7,300 support, setting up the next leg higher. Supports: healthy EPS growth, lower oil (Brent to $75/bbl by 4Q27), more stable rates (Warsh's FOMC tone read as not intensifying a push to get inflation to 2% quickly), broadening AI adoption (44% of S&P 500 companies now cite a quantifiable AI benefit, up from 32%), and a valuation reset to roughly 18x against about 19.5x fair value. MS stays in Quality but rotates more cyclically, naming Industrials its top sector pick, with Financials, Consumer Discretionary and Hyperscalers also attractive. Main risk: more hawkish Fed policy re-tightening financial conditions. Bull case is 10,000, bear case 6,000.
